evidence.observation: the flag byte of each clock programming entry is decoded bit by bit and bit 4 becomes a per-entry boolean; the code that applies a clock offset to the entries was not traced, so that bit 4 marks the entries an offset moves is inferred

evidence.observation: the clocks table DRAM row names the DRAM entries of the clock programming table: one per memory clock the performance states use, rising, flag byte 0x03 or 0x13; bit 4 is set on the top memory levels of every image whose entries take this shape (all but the passive RTX A40) and never on the 405 and 810 MHz idle levels; four GA104/GA106 laptop images (RTX 3060, 3070 and 3080 Laptop GPU) also set it on their intermediate level, which the other images leave clear

fields.label: Memory clock 6001 MHz follows the memory offset
fields.reason: experimental, opt-in: bit 4 of the flag byte of the 6001 MHz memory level in the clock programming table; stock images set it on the top memory levels, and a memory offset that takes the memory below the highest level without it drops it to a lower level instead (on one RTX 3050 Laptop GPU to 810 MHz); setting it was expected to let the offset move this level too (inferred), but on that card, tested on its 5501 MHz level with a lower memory offset floor, the memory still dropped to 810 MHz; the levels with it stay the top ones

evidence.observation: the clocks table GPC row names one clock programming entry whose equation index is the root of the GPC VF curve in the VFE table; the stored GPC frequency deltas of the clocks table are ignored by default and could only raise the curve; a VFE equation adds its next equation to its clamped value (as the voltage equations show), so a constant linked from the root should move every point of the curve (inferred; the curve evaluation was not traced)
evidence.source: GSP-RM firmware 615.78.08 (gsp_ga10x.bin), clocks and clock programming table parsers

evidence.observation: the GPC root is a compare equation with MHz output that no other equation references and that links no next equation; the first unused VFE slot is clean; compare equations with a next link and MHz output are common, and a newer RTX 4090 BIOS fills the older one's first unused slot with a constant equation (a 15 mV voltage constant that links the VMIN equation and that the memory clock programming entries name, see nvvdd_vmin_mv); no image links a constant to the GPC root: two SKUs of one chip (RTX 2080 Ti and TITAN RTX) differ by +45 MHz in the constant term of one polynomial inside the curve's floor and cap, and vendor factory-OC images keep the reference curve
evidence.source: Ada, Ampere and GB20x VBIOS corpus
